_comment: Study A HELD-OUT set (Sprint 24). Authored AFTER the relation polarity matrix was frozen (commit f2df2de) from events disjoint with the 22-event design set. All values verified against sources before inclusion. Summaries are natural news copy — NOT engineered toward the classifier's keyword rules.

events.event_summary: United States special forces raid a compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan, and kill Osama bin Laden, the mastermind of the September 11 attacks. His body is buried at sea within hours as crowds celebrate outside the White House.
events.question: Will the public approve of President Barack Obama's job performance?
events.metric: % approving of President Obama's job performance
events.verification_note: Gallup (news.gallup.com/poll/147437): 46% three days before the operation, 52% three days after.
events.notes: Military-success rally — an archetype the frozen matrix does not cover (no 'victory' event class).

events.event_summary: Militant students storm the United States embassy in Tehran and seize dozens of American diplomats and staff as hostages, parading blindfolded captives before cameras and demanding the extradition of the deposed Shah.
events.question: Will the public approve of President Jimmy Carter's job performance?
events.metric: % approving of President Carter's job performance
events.verification_note: Gallup retrospective (news.gallup.com/opinion/gallup/235277): 32% before the crisis, 38% initially, 51% by late November 1979.

events.event_summary: News breaks that the President had a sexual relationship with a White House intern and may have urged her to lie under oath. An independent counsel expands his investigation as the President publicly denies the allegations.
events.question: Will the public approve of President Bill Clinton's job performance?
events.metric: % approving of President Clinton's job performance
events.verification_note: Gallup via CNN/Newsweek: 59-60% just before the story broke (Jan 1998), 69% at the close of January post-SOTU (news.gallup.com/poll/4609). Pre-story value oscillated 58-60.
events.notes: Scandal-inversion hard case: approval ROSE through the scandal (peaking at 73% after the December impeachment vote).

events.event_summary: Soldiers without insignia take control of Crimea's airports and parliament; within weeks Moscow annexes the peninsula following a hastily organized referendum, and Western governments respond with sanctions.
events.question: Will the public approve of President Vladimir Putin's performance?
events.metric: % of Russians approving of Putin's performance
events.verification_note: Levada via Moscow Times: 65% January 2014 -> 86% June 2014 (87% by August). Window wider than ideal (Jan->Jun).
events.notes: Rally around an incumbent-initiated territorial seizure — the acting side's population, not the attacked side's.

events.event_summary: Kabul falls to the Taliban as the American withdrawal from Afghanistan descends into chaos: desperate crowds swarm the airport runways, and a suicide bombing at the gates kills thirteen American service members and scores of Afghans.
events.question: Will the public approve of President Joe Biden's job performance?
events.metric: % approving of President Biden's job performance
events.verification_note: Gallup: 49% early August 2021 (poll 354017, 'Mostly Pre-Afghanistan Turmoil'), 43% September (poll 391661).
events.notes: Blame for a self-authored operation despite an external attack inside the event — a compound case.

events.event_summary: The coronavirus outbreak is declared a national emergency; states shutter schools and businesses, hospitals brace for a surge of patients, and daily life across the country grinds to a halt within days.
events.question: Will the public approve of President Donald Trump's job performance?
events.metric: % approving of President Trump's job performance
events.verification_note: Gallup (news.gallup.com/poll/298313): 49% Mar 13-22 2020, up from 44% earlier in March — a small crisis rally.

events.event_summary: Britain votes to leave the European Union. The Prime Minister resigns the next morning, the pound crashes to a thirty-one-year low against the dollar, and businesses warn of hiring and investment freezes amid the uncertainty.
events.question: Will consumers be confident about the economy?
events.verification_note: GfK via CNBC/IBTimes: -1 (June 2016) -> -12 (July 2016), sharpest fall since March 1990. Index points, not pp (disclosed, as with UMich events).

events.event_summary: Iraqi forces invade and occupy Kuwait, seizing the emirate's oil fields within hours. Oil prices spike as an international embargo is imposed and hundreds of thousands of troops begin deploying to the Gulf.
events.question: Will consumers be confident about the economy?
events.poll_source: University of Michigan Index of Consumer Sentiment
events.metric: Michigan Index of Consumer Sentiment (index points)
events.verification_note: UMich ICS: Aug 1990 88.2 -> Sept 1990 76.4 (official tbmics table; gas-price shock after the invasion). August reading partially straddles the event.
